definition: The goods, terms, and payment you propose in exchange for a customer's money.
example: Make people an offer so good they would feel stupid saying no.

definition: The act of moving someone to agree, especially by making them feel understood.
example: The point of good persuasion is for the prospect to feel understood.

definition: A potential buyer who has a problem and the means to pay for a solution.
example: The point of good persuasion is for the prospect to feel understood.

definition: A gap between two things that ought to match, here between price and perceived value.
example: This price to value discrepancy is what you need to avoid at all costs.

definition: Priced well above the common market, as a signal of higher value.
example: Premium pricing is not only a smart business decision, but a moral one when it funds a better result.

definition: Judged to be true by the buyer, whether or not the measurement is exact.
example: Increase the perceived likelihood of achievement and the offer grows more valuable.

definition: The chance that a promised result will actually happen.
example: How will I know it is going to happen? That question is the perceived likelihood of achievement.

definition: What the buyer must give up, in effort or comfort, to reach the result.
example: Decrease the perceived effort and sacrifice, and the same dream outcome is worth more.

definition: Smooth and without visible friction from one step to the next.
example: The best companies make the path immediate, seamless, and effortless.

definition: Requiring little strain from the person who wants the result.
example: The best companies in the world focus on making things immediate, seamless, and effortless.

definition: Focused notice; the care a buyer gives something they have paid dearly for.
example: Those who pay the most, pay the most attention.

definition: Money, effort, or stake put into something in the hope of a return.
example: That sting will force their attention and their investment in your product or service.

definition: The work of making a product known to people who do not yet know it exists.
example: Advertising, the process of making known, lets strangers know about the stuff you sell.

definition: The sheer number of repetitions, enough that chance stops deciding the outcome.
example: Volume negates luck when the repetitions pile high enough.

definition: Doing the same useful action again until skill and results show up.
example: You have to do so many repetitions that it would be unreasonable not to be successful.

definition: Beyond what good sense would expect; here, a failure that volume has made absurd.
example: Do so many repetitions that it would be unreasonable not to be successful.

definition: A product so similar to its rivals that buyers compare only the price.
example: If you have a commodity offer, you will compete on price.

definition: The money left after costs, which funds better delivery and growth.
example: When you raise your prices, you multiply your margin because you have money left to invest.

definition: A settled belief strong enough to ask for a serious price.
example: Experience is what gives you the conviction to ask for someone's entire year's salary as payment.

definition: The power to attract; here, the pull of a price that signals something rare.
example: The higher the price, the more allure your product or service has.

definition: A category with no real substitute, so the seller sets the terms.
example: In that new perceived marketplace, you are a monopoly and can make monopoly profits.

definition: Shockingly excessive; he uses it for profit so large it startles people.
example: We are trying to make egregious amounts of money, not stay barely above water.

definition: Having good moral effect; a cycle in which each step improves the next.
example: Raising the price and reinvesting in the buyer is the virtuous cycle of price.

definition: Made distinct from rivals so buyers cannot compare it on price alone.
example: A Grand Slam Offer forces a prospect to assess the value of your differentiated product.
